title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1% above regular)
drivers.evidence: At $4.56, sales were 195 (2026-09-28) and 119 (2026-10-05), both below baseline; 2026-09-28 was ordinary, showing 7% drop. Historical price sensitivity supports ~8% decline.

drivers.name: New competitor across the street
drivers.evidence: Competitor entry in a similar market likely reduces demand. No direct history, but plausible based on competitive dynamics. Shrink toward 1.0 due to uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. The target week has a 5.1% price increase to $4.56, which is above regular price. Historical data shows that price increases reduce demand: at $4.56 (same as 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05), sales were 195 and 119, both below baseline. The 2026-10-05 week was after a promotion, but the 2026-09-28 week (no promotion) saw a 7% drop. The competitor opening across the street introduces a new competitive threat. No promotion or event is scheduled. The classical model suggests no uplift, but judgment overrides this due to price and new competition. The effect is uncertain, so shrink toward 1.0. The price effect is estimated at -8% (based on 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05), and the competitor adds -3% to -5%. Combined, a conservative adjustment is -6% to -8%, shrunk to -7% with medium confidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.2 - 290.7 | 10%-90%: 156.0 - 281.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
